chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fadhl, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Uqayl al-Numayri, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who rented a house that contained a garden, and he planted in the garden, planted date palms and trees and fruits and other things, and did not consult the owner of the house regarding that, he said: 'He bears the rent, and the owner of the house appraises the planting and the grafting at a fair price, and gives it to the planter if he had consulted him regarding that. And if he had not consulted him regarding that, then he bears the rent, and the planting and the crops are his, and he uproots them and takes them wherever he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rights and obligations of a tenant and landlord when improvements are made to rented property without prior consultation?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'iqal' (removal) for unauthorized improvements, prioritizing the tenant's right to reclaim their labor while ensuring the owner is not unjustly enriched. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness in lease contracts, distinguishing between implied consent (where compensation is mandatory) and unilateral action (where removal is permitted). This ruling underpins the concept of 'gharar' avoidance in commercial transactions by clarifying ownership of fixtures.
